stop_recommendation.reasoning: No explicit numeric target was given for this goal, so the read comes from trend and residual evidence rather than a fixed threshold. Val MAE has improved across the run (26.37 -> 21.24 -> 21.48 -> 21.09) and this iteration is confirmed best-so-far with a good_fit overfitting ratio — but the iteration_012 -> iteration_014 improvement was only -1.8% relative, a diminishing-returns signal, and one concrete untried hypothesis still exists (step below). Residual ACF is clean at lag_1/lag_7, so there's no leftover temporal structure pointing to a different problem. Recommend one more targeted iteration before considering this done.
stop_recommendation.binding_constraint_note: not required while the recommendation is 'continue'. A 'stop' recommendation must name the mechanism holding the model back - an unexplained structural break, a segment too small to learn from, signal absent from every source, irreducible noise at this granularity - and 'the metric plateaued' is not one.

diagnosis.primary_issue: A pure trend feature (days_since_start) carries more importance (0.26) than any lag or calendar feature, including the newly-added lag_14 (0.16) — the model may be leaning on a raw time index to compensate for demand structure the current feature set doesn't fully represent, rather than that structure being genuinely absent.
evidence: days_since_start ranks 1st in feature importance (0.2605) despite being the least domain-specific feature available — a raw day counter, not a demand-informed signal
bread_quantity_lag_14 (added this iteration specifically to capture bi-weekly patterns) ranks 2nd (0.16), meaningfully behind the trend feature
no monthly-scale (~28 day) lag or rolling feature exists yet in feature_subset_used — the largest window is rolling_7d_mean

residual ACF is clean at lag_1 and lag_7, meaning weekly structure is well captured — the outsized trend-feature importance is more consistent with missing monthly/seasonal structure than missing weekly structure
diagnosis.root_cause: The engineered feature set has strong weekly-scale coverage (lag_1, lag_7, lag_14, rolling_7d_mean, day-of-week dummies) but no monthly-scale signal, so the model falls back on the raw trend feature to absorb whatever slower-moving pattern exists in demand — a coarser proxy than a purpose-built monthly-scale feature would be.

hypothesis.statement: Adding a bread_quantity_lag_28 and/or a rolling_28d_mean feature should reduce reliance on days_since_start and modestly improve validation MAE, since it would give the model a monthly-scale demand signal instead of forcing the raw trend feature to stand in for it.

suggested_action.action: add bread_quantity_lag_28 (and/or rolling_28d_mean) alongside the existing lag_7/lag_14/rolling_7d_mean features
suggested_action.reasoning: Directly targets the root cause — a monthly-scale gap in an otherwise well-covered weekly-scale feature set — with the same low-risk pattern that worked for lag_14 in iteration_008 (Spearman check first, then include only if it clears the same relevance bar Feature Engineering already applies).

hypothesis.alternative_if_wrong: If lag_28/rolling_28d doesn't reduce days_since_start's importance or improve val MAE, the trend-feature reliance is more likely genuine (a real slow drift in demand, e.g. gradual customer-base growth) rather than a missing-feature artifact — in that case, consider a smoother trend decomposition (e.g. an STL trend component per references/model_selection_timeseries.md) to replace the raw day-index feature instead of adding more lags.

coverage_check._note: Required whenever stop_recommendation is 'stop'. Records the evidence for each condition in the skill's Coverage (breadth) row, so the gate is auditable rather than asserted. tools/stop_check.py evaluates the same conditions mechanically from state/ and history/ and the Planner runs it before end_model - this block is what a reader checks it against.
coverage_check.verdict: no condition blocks a stop. Any non-empty blocks_stop makes stop_recommendation 'continue' regardless of how finished the metrics look, and the blocking item becomes one of this call's ranked hypotheses.

output._field_name_note: stop_recommendation is the contract name. run_20260904T140437Z wrote stop_continue_verdict instead; tools/stop_check.py reads both and flags the drift, but the contract name is authoritative. A gate that reads one name silently passes when a node writes the other.

hypotheses_retired._note: Required whenever stop_recommendation is 'stop'. One entry per hypothesis any Diagnosis call in this run ranked, INCLUDING earlier calls' lower-ranked ones. Every entry must be retired by one of three routes. An estimate of expected gain is not a route: predicting the result is what running the test replaces.
